subsystems.name: Compliant body
subsystems.role: the part that bends, stretches or inflates instead of using rigid joints.

subsystems.name: Actuation
subsystems.role: supplies the force without metal gears.
parts: pneumatic supply and miniature proportional valves

subsystems.name: Sensing
subsystems.role: lets the controller know how hard it is squeezing and where the object is.

subsystems.name: Control
subsystems.role: soft bodies are hard to model, so control leans on feedback and learning.

subsystems.name: Mounting and tooling
subsystems.role: connects the soft effector to a standard industrial arm.

buildSteps.title: Pick the compliance principle
buildSteps.detail: Decide whether the part should inflate (pneumatic chambers), bend (fibre-reinforced fingers, including fin-ray-style designs that curl around an object), stiffen on demand (granular jamming), or be cable-driven through a soft core.

buildSteps.title: Model and simulate
buildSteps.detail: Because silicone does not behave like steel, the design is checked with hyperelastic material models and large-deformation simulation rather than simple rigid-body analysis, and the mould is designed at the same time.

buildSteps.title: Make the mould
buildSteps.detail: A mould is machined, or 3D-printed for small runs, sometimes as a lost-core or two-part tool that can be pulled out of undercut chambers.

buildSteps.title: Cast the elastomer
buildSteps.detail: Two-part platinum-cure silicone is mixed, degassed under vacuum to remove bubbles, poured or injected, and cured in an oven; multi-material parts are cast in successive pours with surface treatment or overmoulding between layers so the layers bond.

buildSteps.title: Add reinforcement and sensors
buildSteps.detail: Fibre wraps, fabric plies or a stiffer second elastomer are laid in to control the direction of bending, and conductive elastomer channels or flexible strain gauges are cast into the body.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and plumb
buildSteps.detail: Fingers are bonded to a rigid base, tubing and valves are connected, and the effector is fitted to the robot wrist.

buildSteps.title: Characterise
buildSteps.detail: The gripper is tested for force-versus-displacement, grip on different shapes and surfaces, cycle life, tear resistance and creep, and the results are written into the controller.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the control loop
buildSteps.detail: Grasp policies are tuned by demonstration or learning, with vision and pressure feedback closing the loop on a standard industrial arm.

buildSteps.title: Validate in production
buildSteps.detail: The cell is qualified for the real line — cycle time, contamination, washdown or cleanroom compatibility, and human-robot safety limits.

prerequisites.why: the whole approach depends on tough, fatigue-resistant silicone and polyurethane that bond reliably in layers.
inflatable grippers need fast, precise pressure control, not just on/off air.
sensors that survive millions of stretch cycles are still the weak point of most soft machines.
infinite degrees of freedom make classic robot control inadequate; learning-based methods help but need data.
force and pressure limits for contact with people set the rules that let soft effectors work alongside workers.

pathway.milestone: commercial soft and compliant grippers handling food, glass, fabric and packed goods
pathway.unlocks: automation of pick-and-place tasks that rigid jaws bruise or crush.

pathway.milestone: soft arms and hands with integrated sensing working in shared cells
pathway.unlocks: assembly and inspection steps that mix human judgement with machine repeatability.

pathway.milestone: on-demand stiffening (jamming, fibre or fluid) so one effector can be soft for gripping and rigid for pushing
pathway.unlocks: fewer tool changes and wider task range per robot.

pathway.milestone: self-modelling soft robots that learn their own shape and adapt through wear
pathway.unlocks: durable, general-purpose soft manipulators rather than single-task grippers.
